thread:
incident-bot: Severity P1 detected for cluster tp-pool-7 - sustained KV cache growth triggering node-level paging and NCCL stall signals. Auto-alerting oncall.

maria (oncall): seeing huge 95p latency spike in prod - metrics show continuous-batch request queueing. paging rate up on gpunode-17. :fire:

devin (sre): confirming, pmap shows swap usage > 70% on gpunode-17 and gpunode-18. NCCL error rate rising. attaching logs.

liam (eng-runtime): logs: ```
[2026-06-12T03:20:05Z] kv_cache: shard_map mismatch detected: expected 8 parts, got 6
[2026-06-12T03:20:11Z] batcher: continuous_batcher backlog +1200 requests
[2026-06-12T03:20:12Z] nccl: op timeout, rank 2 -> rank 5
```

anjali (eng-ml): looks like tensor-parallel KV sharding slipped after the recent kernel pick that changed ordering. Could cause uneven partitions -> some shards blow past memory thresholds and trigger cascading evictions causing batch blowup.

maria (oncall): customer impact? jess can you surface support tickets?

jess (support): two active incidents from Acme and BrightEdge. Both report 500s and big latency. Customers on dedicated tp-pool-7.

devin (sre): immediate mitigation options: 1) disable continuous batching globally, 2) force-evict large prefixes on hot shards, 3) scale short-term by adding standby nodes, 4) fallback routing to non-tp model variant.

maria (oncall): prioritize minimal blast radius. Step 1 disable continuous batching for tp-pool-7. I'll run the toggle.

liam (eng-runtime): howto:
```
# disable continuous batching for pool
curl -X POST "https://control-plane/api/pools/tp-pool-7/config" -d '{"continuous_batching": false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```

maria (oncall): done. control-plane returned 200. batch queue draining slowly. monitor.

(5m later)

devin (sre): batch backlog down from 1200 -> 180. swap usage still high on gpunode-17, but NCCL stalls reduced.

anjali (eng-ml): we should also evict long KV prefixes to free space quickly. Propose TTL-based purge for top 3 hot prefixes on affected shards.

liam (eng-runtime): running purge script on shard owners. Command:
```
kubectl exec -it kv-ops -- /bin/bash -lc "python tools/kv_purge.py --pool tp-pool-7 --prefixes 'user_prompt:' 'session:' 'longctx:' --force"
```

maria (oncall): running with --force now.

(2m)

incident-bot: Deploy job kv-purge-job-180000 started by maria (oncall).

jess (support): customer Acme reporting improved response times for some endpoints. BrightEdge still seeing intermittent errors.

devin (sre): gpunode-18 still has an outlier partition with 3x expected KV size. I think sharding mapping is wrong for rank assignment on that kernel. We need a short-term mapping override to rebalance.

liam (eng-runtime): we're preparing a hotfix to remap affected model instances to correct TP shard counts. Patch ready: update shard_map to force even partitioning and restart the kv-daemon on affected pods.

anjali (eng-ml): quick validation: run local check to ensure all replicas report expected shard sizes:
```
python tools/check_shards.py --pool tp-pool-7 --expect 8
```

devin (sre): recommend rolling restart with 1-per-second delay to avoid NCCL collective freeze. Use annotation to skip heavy traffic nodes.

maria (oncall): proceed with controlled restart. Oncall to coordinate with liam.

liam (eng-runtime): starting rollout: ``kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-daemon -n tp-pool-7 --max-surge=1``

(rollout messages)

incident-bot: deployment/kv-daemon rollout started by liam (eng-runtime).

(10m pass)

devin (sre): nodes restarting sequentially. NCCL errors gone from logs. swap falling back to baseline. batch backlog nearly zero.

jess (support): BrightEdge confirms errors resolved: "we're back to normal". Acme fully recovered. :thumbsup:

maria (oncall): post-mitigation checks: run eval prompt set and perf tests for tail latency.

anjali (eng-ml): running evals: 1000 prompts, 99th p latency dropped from 850ms -> 210ms on the tp-pool-7 path. Quality unchanged. No regressed outputs in smoke tests.

liam (eng-runtime): root cause summary draft: recent kernel/kernsel change altered deterministic ordering used by our TP shard mapper for KV cache. This led to uneven partition sizes after model warmup, causing some ranks to exceed memory and trigger paging and NCCL timeouts. Continuous batching amplified the effect by piling requests onto hot shards.

maria (oncall): next steps: roll permanent fix to kernel selection logic, add stronger invariants in shard mapper test, enable an emergency circuit breaker to auto-disable continuous batching per-pool when any node hits swap>50% and batch backlog > 300.

devin (sre): also add alerting: if KV shard size > 2x expected for >2min -> auto-reroute and notify oncall.

liam (eng-runtime): scheduled hotfix PR: #1728. Will run canary in tp-pool-7 staging then prod tomorrow 02:00 UTC. Will add canary metrics dashboard.

jess (support): I'll draft a customer incident summary and outreach for Acme and BrightEdge, include mitigation timeline and root cause.

maria (oncall): final state: continuous batching disabled (manual unset required), kv shard mapper patched in canary, backlog drained, customers recovered. Keeping channel open for 1h for followups. Thanks all.

ops-rot: ack. I'll pick this up next shift if anything flares.

incident-bot: Incident P1 resolved (mitigated) by actions: disable-batching, kv-purge, shard-remap-rollout at 1800004830.

maria (oncall): closing thread but will create postmortem doc and link here once ready.
